The rating reflects the standards found on the date of the inspection and does not reflect the quality of the food. Businesses have the right to appeal a rating, to publish a reply alongside it, and to request a re-inspection once improvements have been made, so a rating listed here may since have changed. Each business's current rating is on the Food Standards Agency website.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale takeaway hails 'incredible honour' as it's declared North West's best
candidates.source_summary: "From our kitchen in Littleborough to the national stage, this achievement marks a truly special moment in our journey"
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Greater Manchester takeaway has said winning a big award is a "major honour". Last month, The Rochdale restaurant was named a Regional Top Ten Finalist as part of the Asian Restaurant & Takeaway Awards (ARTA). Now, Tandoori Flames in Littleborough revealed that they've taken home the coveted North West Regional Takeaway of the Year prize. The restaurant, which boasts a five-star rating on Just Eat, offers a range of traditional Indian food, fried chicken, as well as tandoori, Balti, masala and biryani dishes. Speaking about the win on social media, the team told its followers that they had a "win worth celebrating" and said it was an "incredible honour" for the entire team to enjoy. Click here for the latest on Manchester's food & drink scene, gigs and more in our CityLife newsletter They added: "This prestigious award celebrates our passion for authentic Indian flavours, dedication to quality and commitment to serving delicious food to our wonderful customers. From our kitchen in Littleborough to the national stage, this achievement marks a truly special moment in our journey. "And the biggest thank you goes to YOU! To every customer who has ordered from us, recommended us to friends and family, and supported our takeaway over the years, we're incredibly grateful. "Your loyalty and encouragement inspire us to keep doing what we love. A huge thank you also goes to our hardworking team, whose dedication has made this achievement possible. "We're proud to bring this award home to Littleborough and share this fantastic milestone with our community!" The restaurant on Church Street prides itself on using traditional recipes, aromatic spices, and carefully selected ingredients. Customers can choose from a range of sizzling tandoori starters, rich curries and freshly prepared Balti dishes. Its standard starters range from samosa and Reshmi Kebab, to garlic fish and onion bhaji, as well as king prawns, chicken chaat and paneer pakora. Tandoori starters include tandoori chicken, lamb tikka, seekh kebab and tandoori wings. They also have a 'Choice of Excellence' menu which includes Murgi Masala, which encompasses t andoori chicken off the bone cooked with minced lamb, and Nawabi chops, which sees lamb chops cooked with onions, pimientos and green peppers in a medium spiced sauce. They have a wide selection of special Balti dishes too. including Gorom with green chilli and hot spices for curry addicts. Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , a spokesperson for the takeaway said: "To me, winning isn’t just about taking home a trophy; it’s about the hard work, dedication and passion that go into every single day. It’s about overcoming challenges, believing in what we do and striving to be the best we can be. "Being nominated for the Curry Award in the North West means so much to us. It recognises the commitment, teamwork and determination that go into everything we do. None of this would be possible without our amazing staff, whose hard work, loyalty and passion make a difference every single day, and our wonderful customers, who continue to support us and make what we do worthwhile. "We are truly grateful to every member of our team and every customer who has been part of our journey. candidates.source_title: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Plans for a direct rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to improve the rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again. Today, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays . Among those backing calls for the extra services was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who called Lumo’s bid to restore six daily direct services between Rochdale and the capital a “game-changing opportunity” for the borough and the wider North West. But the ORR rejected the plans after its assessment found adding more trains to the West Coast Main Line — which also included services to Blackpool and Wrexham — would likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers. It said its assessment following detailed and extensive analysis is that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the West Coast Main Line has not materially changed since it rejected a similar application by Lumo last year. An external review commissioned by ORR also supported this conclusion. READ MORE: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ The ORR said gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers.

candidates.source_title: Huge queue as SpudBros launch Rochdale store - and delighted schoolgirl wins a trolley dash - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_summary: Predictably, the SpudBros brothers caused a bit of a stir with another Greater Manchester store launch - with queues of hungry punters, and a lucky youngster winning a special prize after a five-hour wait
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A queue of hungry punters headed out to Rochdale as SpudBros launched their latest new express store serving up their signature loaded jacket potatoes. With millions of followers on social media, the SpudBros phenomenon continues to grow with Lancashire brothers Jacob and Harley Nelson steering the expansion. The duo, who first started out with one tram on Preston's Flag Market, launched their 21st new SpudBros Express store in partnership with the EG station on Manchester New Road on Tuesday. Huge queues formed after the brothers announced the first 100 people would get a free spud on opening day. Not only that, but there was a special surprise awaiting the very first person in the queue - who was Rochdale schoolgirl Isla Lawrence. Click here for the latest on Manchester's food & drink scene, gigs and more in our CityLife newsletter 11-year-old Isla and mum Jackie had queued from 7am on the day to be the first served up a spud by Jacob and Harley themselves. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A school is changing the way it celebrates success and achievements following concerns about innocent images of children being turned into sexualised content. The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) and the National Crime Agency (NCA) have seen a national increase in online offenders exploiting publicly available images of children to create realistic sexual content. The IWF found 3,440 AI-generated videos of child sexual abuse in 2025, compared to just 13 in 2024, and the NCA has increasingly seen offenders using AI technologies to target children in sinister new ways. Following updated guidance from both organisations, Cardinal Langley RC High School in Middleton says it will continue to celebrate achievements of students, but will make changes to reduce the risk of altered images. In a letter to parents, deputy headteacher Angela Williams said: “The dignity and wellbeing of every young person entrusted to our care sits at the heart of our safeguarding responsibilities. Those responsibilities also require us to respond when technology changes and new risks emerge. We are therefore making an important change to the way we use photographs of pupils online. “Artificial intelligence technology has developed extremely rapidly. One consequence is that an ordinary photograph placed on a website or social-media platform can potentially be copied and used by another person to create convincing AI altered imagery. The person in the original photograph does not need to have given permission and may have no knowledge that their image has been used. Cardinal Langley will look at different ways to celebrate students’ success “Recent national safeguarding guidance for education settings has consequently encouraged schools to reconsider how identifiable images of children and young people are made publicly available online.

candidates.source_title: New Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre takes shape in Rochdale - The Manufacturer
candidates.source_summary: A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale, which is set to become a nationally significant gateway driving the development of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster in the region. The 30,000 sq. ft centre is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub for advanced materials and manufacturing in Rochdale, bringing together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners in one location. AVID provides an environment where organisations can innovate, grow and commercialise new technologies, strengthening Greater Manchester’s position as a leading centre for advanced materials and manufacturing. Completion of the building represents a major milestone for years of partnership working between Rochdale Development Agency (RDA), Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners. RDA has led the physical development of the SMMC, working with partners to secure investment and position advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority opportunity for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The next phase will see work move from construction towards specialist fit-out ahead of bringing the centre into operation in 2027. The RDA brought together partners from industry, academia and government to establish the Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) in 2023. Since then, businesses have been able to connect with a national network of specialist expertise, facilities and innovation support through the CEAMS partners, including The University of Manchester, the Henry Royce Institute, National Physical Laboratory (NPL), Centre for Process Innovation (CPI) and NCC (formerly National Composites Centre). CEAMS has already supported more than 90 companies, developing new products and processes and demonstrating the value of a more connected innovation ecosystem.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council is preparing to implement revised planning decision procedures from October 31, with more applications to be decided by planning officers rather than elected committees under new Government guidance for councils across England.The changes follow the Town and Country Planning Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions England Regulations 2026 and aim to allow committees to focus on major proposals while officers handle more routine cases, according to a council report.Under the new system, applications will be divided into two schedules. Schedule One cases, including householder applications, minor commercial and minor residential proposals, lawful development certificates and technical matters, must be determined by planning officers.Schedule Two applications can be referred to the planning committee, including larger developments, listed building consent, advertisement consent, tree preservation order consent and legal agreements with developers. However, referrals require agreement between a nominated councillor and nominated officer.A council report said the Government wants planning committees to have a clearer role focused on significant proposals while technical and smaller decisions are handled by officers."The Government’s aim is to provide greater clarity and consistency regarding the role of planning committees in decision-making, so that committees focus on key proposals that matter to an area while more minor and technical decisions are made by planning officers." said Rochdale Council in its report.The report also stated that councillors will still be able to engage with planning matters, raise residents’ concerns and submit material planning reasons. However, a councillor request alone will not require an application to be considered by the committee.Ward councillors will no longer be able to automatically call applications into committee meetings, and the previous threshold based on the number of objections received will also no longer trigger committee consideration.The council report warned that decisions could face legal challenges if a planning committee determines an application that regulations require officers to decide. candidates.source_summary: Almost six in 10 people across Greater Manchester have kept debt secret from their partner, according to research commissioned by Manchester Credit Union.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Almost six in 10 people across Greater Manchester have kept debt secret from their partner, according to research commissioned by Manchester Credit Union. The Greater Manchester Money Report surveyed 5,008 adults across the region, including Rochdale, Bury and Bolton. The credit union said 59% had kept debt from their partner. Its findings also showed that 67% had some form of debt, while 10% were struggling to repay it. Among those who had kept debt secret, 47% had undisclosed debts of between £1,000 and £20,000. The most common amount was £5,000 to £10,000, reported by 17%. Family and friends were the most common source of help people said they would approach during financial difficulty. They were chosen by 38%, compared with 18% who would turn to a bank. Mandy Wilcock, chief executive of Manchester Credit Union, said “There should be no shame in asking for help with money. Financial pressures can affect anyone, particularly when the cost of everyday essentials continues to strain household budgets.” She called for greater financial education and better signposting to advice. Censuswide carried out the survey between 28 April and 20 May 2026. It covered adults aged 18 and over in all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs, with results weighted by age, gender and borough.

candidates.source_summary: Darrell Clarke wants Tranmere to be ‘more clinical’ after Rochdale draw Bicester Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Manager Darrell Clarke believes Tranmere need an injection of confidence after spurning an array of opportunities in the 1-1 home draw with Rochdale at Prenton Park. Tom Conlon opened the scoring for Rovers before Clarke saw the hosts pegged back in the second half by Dajaune Brown’s strike after missing multiple chances to go two in front. The 48-year-old cut a frustrated figure after the match and said: “We’ve only got ourselves to blame because we have to be more clinical. There were loads of opportunities and we didn’t take them. “What you can’t do is beat them with a stick. We have to give them the confidence that things will come good. “They have to work hard and produce more of those moments in training, but we’re disappointed.” The result marks Tranmere’s sixth draw of the season, and Clarke believes there are no excuses as to why they’re not higher in the table. “We’ve got 12 points in 10 games, and we feel we should be on a lot more,” he added. “But it’s a results business and we can’t feel sorry for ourselves. If we take our chances, it makes games easier because then teams open up a bit more. “Things become tense as we get frustrated, but at the end of the day we have to finish our chances and I’m as disappointed as the supporters right now.”

candidates.source_title: Free half-term activities and meals offered to eligible children in Bury
candidates.source_summary: Eligible children in Bury can access free activities and healthy meals this half term through the council’s expanded Holiday Activities and Food Programme.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Eligible children in Bury can access free activities and healthy meals this half term through the council’s expanded Holiday Activities and Food Programme. The offer comes after the school holiday food voucher scheme ended following changes to government funding guidance. Bury Council said it has expanded the Holiday Activities and Food Programme, known as HAF, to provide more opportunities across the borough. Funded by the UK Government and co-ordinated by the council, the programme supports children and young people eligible for benefits-related free school meals. Activities include sports, arts and crafts, outdoor activities and wellbeing sessions, alongside healthy meals. Eligible families will automatically receive a HAF voucher through the Holiday Activities App. Parents and carers will receive an email or text message explaining how to access their account and book activities and food provision. The council is encouraging families to check their messages and book early. The separate school holiday food voucher scheme has ended following changes to government guidance on the use of the Crisis and Resilience Fund. Term-time free school meals are unaffected and will continue as normal.

candidates.source_title: £13 million Millwood Primary School expansion officially opened in Bury
candidates.source_summary: A £13 million expansion at Millwood Primary School has been officially opened, allowing the Bury school to cater for more than 200 primary-aged pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A £13 million expansion at Millwood Primary School has been officially opened, allowing the Bury school to cater for more than 200 primary-aged pupils with special educational needs and disabilities. The new wing includes seven classrooms, a multi-use hall, sensory rooms and a rebound room. The project also delivered external play spaces, additional parking and repairs to the school’s roof and existing building. Funding came through Department for Education capital allocations supporting councils to provide school places for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities, known as SEND. Bury Council said the expansion responds to increasing demand for specialist places and will allow more children to attend school closer to home. Councillor Sandra Walmsley, cabinet member for children and young people, officially opened the wing and toured the facilities. She was joined by director of education Ben Dunne and head of service for SEND Wendy Young. Councillor Walmsley said, “This investment represents a major step forward in our commitment to improving SEND provision in Bury. The new wing provides outstanding facilities that will make a real difference to children and young people aged 5-11, giving them access to specialist support and learning environments that help them flourish. “It was a privilege to officially open the new wing and see first-hand the fantastic facilities that have been created. Millwood is an exceptional school, and this expansion will allow even more local families to benefit from the high-quality education, care and support it provides.” More information about the school is available at www.millwoodprimaryschool.co.uk .

candidates.source_title: Bury Beer Festival returns to The Met this November
candidates.source_summary: Bury Beer Festival will return to The Met on Friday 6 and Saturday 7 November, with local breweries, food and DJs across four sessions.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Bury Beer Festival will return to The Met on Friday 6 and Saturday 7 November, with local breweries, food and DJs across four sessions. The event takes place in Derby Hall, with sessions starting at midday and 6pm on both days. Brightside Brewing Company, Brewsmith Beer, Tun Brewing Company, Wakey Wakey Brew Company and Vocation Brewery are among the breweries announced. Further breweries are due to be confirmed. Visitors will be able to choose from cask ales, keg beers and small-batch brews. A cider and perry bar will also be available, alongside gin, wine, cocktails and non-alcoholic drinks. Fratelli’s will serve New York-style pizza throughout the weekend, while local DJs provide the music. The Met will use branded festival glasses instead of plastic glasses as part of its efforts to reduce its environmental impact. The festival is the venue’s biggest annual fundraiser. The Met is a registered charity, with ticket sales supporting its work with local communities, artists and audiences. Tickets cost £9, with £8 tickets for CAMRA members and £5 tickets for Met members. Met member discounts are applied automatically at checkout, while CAMRA discounts are available through the venue’s ticket office.

candidates.source_title: New support for survivors of child sexual abuse or exploitation - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Survivors of abuse and exploitation are being offered help to understand their options relating to investigations into allegations they made.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Survivors of abuse and exploitation are being offered help to understand their options relating to investigations into allegations they made. IAmReady.org offers victims and survivors specialist advice and guidance depending on their individual needs and requirements, to help them make informed decisions about their cases. Designed in collaboration with victims and survivors of child sexual abuse and exploitation, the new website provides trauma-informed and accessible information in one place. Users are able to move through the website at their own pace, with natural breaks and options to save their progress and return whenever they feel ready. There is also a feature which enables them to leave the website quickly and replace it with a completely unrelated website for privacy. As well as advice, guidance and support, the website also offers victims and survivors the opportunity to request a review of their case, if it was previously closed as a result of a Crown Prosecution Service or local police force decision, either through the Victims’ Right to Review (VRR) or the Child Sexual Abuse Review Panel (CSARP), and also whether it falls within the scope of Operation Beaconport. Set up in November 2025 following the publication of Baroness Casey’s audit of group-based child sexual abuse and exploitation, Operation Beaconport is reviewing hundreds of cases where a decision to take no further action was made between January 1, 2010, and March 31, 2025. READ MORE: Affordable homes plan refused over harm to Green Belt If a victim and survivor wishes to submit information about a case involving group-based offending that was previously closed, this request will be received and reviewed by specially trained officers from Operation Beaconport. Anyone submitting information about a case has the option to receive updates regarding their request.

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale-London train idea rejected as West Coast Main Line under 'significant pressure' Business Live
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The decision to axe the idea for trains between Rochdale and London Euston is 'disappointing', says the town's MP and rail operator. The idea to have four daily return services between Rochdale and London was rejected by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR). The reason given was that the additional services could 'increase the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers'. Low-cost rail operator Lumo had hoped to start services by 2028, with the plans receiving the backing of Rochdale MP Paul Waugh. Both shared their disappointment following the announcement. Paul Waugh, Rochdale's MP, said: "I am deeply disappointed that the ORR has rejected the proposal for a direct Rochdale to London service. I know how much this would have meant to people in Rochdale and the wider borough, and I remain committed to improving our connections with both Manchester and London. "There are reasons to be hopeful about the future. The Bee Network is bringing greater integration of local rail services across Greater Manchester from 2028 onwards, while the government is progressing Northern Powerhouse Rail and has set out its long-term intention to develop a new rail connection between Birmingham and Manchester to increase capacity on the West Coast Main Line. "These are important investments in our rail network, and I will continue to make the case for Rochdale to benefit from better and more reliable transport links, including to London." The ORR explained that gaps in the current timetable provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers. The government body concluded that adding more services into these windows would reduce that resilience and increase risk of disruption. The ORR also rejected the application of Wrexham, Shropshire & Midlands Railway Company (WSMR) for four return Wrexham-London Euston services and Avanti West Coast's application for additional Blackpool-Euston services. A spokesperson for FirstGroup , who run the Lumo operation, said: "We are disappointed that the ORR has declined our revised application for new Lumo services between London and Rochdale, and we are considering our next steps. "Following the initial decision, we amended our plans in line with feedback and believe the revised proposal demonstrated strong economic benefits for passengers and communities. "It would have delivered the benefits of competition, including greater choice, lower fares and new opportunities for growth across Manchester and the north west . "Open access services have an important role to play in improving connectivity, attracting more people to rail and supporting economic development, all at no cost to the public purse. "We remain convinced that this route offered a compelling case for investment and long-term benefits for communities, businesses and the wider regional economy." ORR has approved access for Avanti's weekday 19:29 Chester to Euston service to carry passengers until December 2030. Stephanie Tobyn, ORR's director of strategy, policy and reform, said: "New services, destinations and greater choice can bring real benefits for passengers and communities. candidates.source_title: Tranmere Rovers v Rochdale: League Two stats & head-to-head - BBC
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale extend their unbeaten League Two run to five games with a 1-1 draw against Tranmere at Prenton Park.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale extended their unbeaten League Two run to five games with a 1-1 draw against Tranmere at Prenton Park. Dajaune Brown's second-half strike cancelled out Tom Conlon's early wonder goal to continue Dale's impressive run of form while Rovers are now winless in their last five after a sixth draw of the season. Conlon gave the hosts the lead on 15 minutes after Rochdale allowed the ball to go out for a Rovers throw-in, and the midfielder capitalised on that error by driving home into the top-left corner from 25 yards. Tranmere ought to have led by more at the break as Tom Ince spurned a glorious chance inside the six-yard box before Dylan Jones fired wide under pressure from Aden Flint on the stroke of half-time. Those misses proved costly when Brown latched on to Charlie Tasker's cross to tap home from close range on 57 minutes. Ince then saw his long-range effort cannon off the underside of the bar as Rovers sought to restore their lead, but Rochdale hung on to pick up another point on the road. Match ends, Tranmere Rovers 1, Rochdale 1. Second Half ends, Tranmere Rovers 1, Rochdale 1.
